TExam traps

BET intercept

If the plotted axis does not start at zero, extrapolate the line to p/p0=0p/p_0 = 0p/p0​=0. And vm=1/(I+s)v_m = 1/(I+s)vm​=1/(I+s), not 1/I1/I1/I.

Radius or diameter?

Sv=6/dp=3/RS_v = 6/d_p = 3/RSv​=6/dp​=3/R. Tutorial 1 Q2's key uses 100 μm\mu\mathrm{m}μm as radius. Say which you assume.

VgV_gVg​ per gram, porosity per volume

εp=Vgρp\varepsilon_p = V_g\rho_pεp​=Vg​ρp​, never VgV_gVg​ alone. In bidisperse pellets, εμ\varepsilon_\muεμ​ per pellet uses ρP\rho_PρP​, per particle uses ρp\rho_pρp​.

Site balance for dissociative adsorption

Count every adsorbed fragment: Ct=Cv+CC⋅S+CO⋅S=Cv(1+2KP)C_t = C_v + C_{C\cdot S} + C_{O\cdot S} = C_v(1 + 2\sqrt{KP})Ct​=Cv​+CC⋅S​+CO⋅S​=Cv​(1+2KP​).

Limiting species leaves the denominator

If adsorption of A limits, CA⋅SC_{A\cdot S}CA⋅S​ is not KAPACvK_AP_AC_vKA​PA​Cv​; it is found from the downstream equilibria, so KAPAK_AP_AKA​PA​ does not appear.

Gas-phase species in site balances

Eley–Rideal reactants and non-adsorbing products (propylene, methane, H2\mathrm{H_{2}}H2​ in toluene) never enter the site balance.

Rate constant basis in MTM_TMT​

Use the constant per pellet volume. k′×ρck' \times\rho_ck′×ρc​ first. k′′k''k′′ (per area) must be multiplied by SaρcS_a\rho_cSa​ρc​.

Levenspiel LLL vs Fogler RRR

Sphere: MTM_TMT​ uses R/3R/3R/3; ϕ1\phi_1ϕ1​ uses RRR. ϕ1=3MT\phi_1 = 3M_Tϕ1​=3MT​. Strong limit MT>4M_T>4MT​>4 is ϕ1>12\phi_1>12ϕ1​>12.

pH2p_{H_2}pH2​​ is not pH2p_H^2pH2​

Subscript 2 is part of the species name.

Temperature and diffusion

Raising TTT raises kkk much more than DeD_eDe​ or kmk_mkm​: transport limits get worse, not better.

MMock mid-semester paper (90 minutes, 50 marks)

Attempt all. Solutions: the linked practice problems and theory sections.

  1. (10 marks)
    1. Distinguish intrinsic and global rates. Derive the global rate for a first-order reaction on a non-porous catalyst with external mass transfer, and sketch concentration profiles for reaction and diffusion control. (5) see M1 §2
    2. Tabulate six differences between physisorption and chemisorption, and say which is used to measure total area and which active area. (3) see M1 §8
    3. Define promoter, inhibitor and poison with one example each. (2) see M1 §7
  2. (10 marks) Problem P1 (BET) and Problem P2 (He–Hg). see P1, see P2
  3. (12 marks)
    1. For cumene ⇌\rightleftharpoons⇌ benzene + propylene, derive the rate law when desorption of benzene is rate-limiting and sketch the initial rate vs PC0P_{C0}PC0​. (6) see M2 §7
    2. Problem P8. (6) see P8
  4. (8 marks) From the toluene data (Table 10-6), explain which species adsorb and why, and propose a mechanism with its rate law. see M2 §11
  5. (10 marks)
    1. Formulate (do not solve) the steady-state diffusion–reaction problem for an nth-order reaction in a spherical pellet: shell balance, flux, rate law, ODE, boundary conditions, dimensionless form, Thiele modulus. Define η\etaη. (5) see M3 §8
    2. Problem P10. (5) see P10

R30 rapid-fire questions

1. What does a catalyst change and not change?

Changes rate (activation energy, mechanism) and selectivity; not ΔH\Delta HΔH, ΔG\Delta GΔG or equilibrium.

2. Which steps disappear for a non-porous catalyst?

Steps 2 and 6 (internal diffusion).

3. Why is a non-catalytic gas–solid reaction inherently transient?

The solid reactant is consumed, so the geometry and rate change with time.

4. Name the three electronic classes of catalysts with an example each.

Conductors (Pt, Ni), semiconductors (NiO, ZnO), insulators/solid acids (silica–alumina).

5. Wet vs dry impregnation?

Wet: excess solution, diffusion. Dry (incipient wetness): exactly pore volume, diffusion plus capillary flow.

6. Why reduce Ni catalyst inside the reactor?

To avoid contact with air and other gases that would poison the reactive nickel.

7. Which poison type does coke represent?

Deposited (and a diffusion poison when it blocks pore mouths); partly reversible by burning.

8. Which Langmuir assumption do Temkin and Freundlich relax?

Constant heat of adsorption (uniform surface).

9. What is the physical meaning of the BET constant ccc?

c=exp⁡[(E1−EL)/RT]c = \exp[(E_1 - E_L)/RT]c=exp[(E1​−EL​)/RT]: how much more strongly the first layer is held than later (liquid-like) layers.

10. Why nitrogen at its boiling point for BET?

It physisorbs on any surface, builds multilayers, is cheap, and its molecular area (16.2 A˚2\mathrm{\text{Å}^{2}}A˚2) is well established.

11. Why does helium measure solid volume?

It enters all pores but not the solid, and hardly adsorbs.

12. What does high pelleting pressure do to macropores and micropores?

Squeezes out macropores (1.08 to 0.265 cm3/g\mathrm{cm^{3}/g}cm3/g) with little change to micropores or area.

13. Isotherm type with a hysteresis loop?

Type IV (and V): capillary condensation in mesopores.

14. Units of KAK_AKA​ (adsorption) and KSK_SKS​ (single site)?

KAK_AKA​: 1/atm. KSK_SKS​: dimensionless (single and dual site); 1/atm for Eley–Rideal.

15. How does KAK_AKA​ vary with temperature, and why?

Decreases: adsorption is exothermic; k−Ak_{-A}k−A​ grows faster with TTT than kAk_AkA​.

16. Initial rate independent of pressure — which step limits?

Desorption.

17. Why is propylene absent from the cumene site balance?

It is not adsorbed; it leaves directly to the gas in the surface reaction.

18. What fraction of heterogeneous reactions are surface-reaction-limited?

More than 75 % (Fogler: 75–80 %).

19. What does an adsorbing inert do to the rate law?

Adds KIPIK_IP_IKI​PI​ to the denominator, lowering the rate.

20. Why can a rate law fit never prove a mechanism?

Several mechanisms can give statistically indistinguishable fits; spectroscopy is needed. A misfit can disprove one.

21. Why does a fluidised bed use the CSTR equation?

The particles are well mixed, so the whole bed sees the exit composition; pressure drop is negligible.

22. Levenspiel's five factors?

Surface kinetics, pore diffusion, particle ΔT\Delta TΔT, film ΔT\Delta TΔT, film diffusion.

23. Why does Levenspiel prefer first-order kinetics for design?

Mechanisms are hard to prove and multi-constant forms cannot easily be combined with diffusion resistances; simple forms fit most data.

24. Boundary condition at the sealed end of a pore?

No flux: dCA/dx=0dC_A/dx = 0dCA​/dx=0 at x=Lx = Lx=L.

25. Characteristic length of a 6 mm diameter cylinder (long)?

L=R/2=1.5L = R/2 = 1.5L=R/2=1.5 mm.

26. η=0.1\eta = 0.1η=0.1 for spheres. Levenspiel MTM_TMT​? Fogler ϕ1\phi_1ϕ1​?

Strong resistance: MT≈10M_T\approx10MT​≈10, ϕ1=3MT≈30\phi_1 = 3M_T\approx30ϕ1​=3MT​≈30.

27. What happens to the Arrhenius plot when pore diffusion takes over?

The slope roughly halves: Eobs≈Etrue/2E_{obs}\approx E_{true}/2Eobs​≈Etrue​/2.

28. Zero-order reaction under strong pore resistance appears as?

Half order.

29. In the Fogler shell balance, why does the flux come out negative?

Flux is defined positive outward (increasing rrr) while A diffuses inward.

30. Where should Pt be placed in a pellet with a very large Thiele modulus?

Only in a thin outer shell: the interior never sees reactant.
